description:
Frank is 52 and has $40,000 sitting in a savings account. To him, the stock market is a casino. His sister Diane, a school librarian who never earned much, has put a little into the market every month since her thirties. Today her account is worth more than Frank's house.

description:

title: How the Super-Rich Legally Hide Billions in Offshore Trusts

description:
Dave runs a small plumbing business and pays his taxes every quarter. Victor has a yacht, a mansion in London and a ski chalet in the Alps, and on paper he owns none of it. The yacht belongs to a company in the British Virgin Islands. The company belongs to a trust in the Cook Islands. And most of it is perfectly legal.

In this video we take offshore trusts apart: what a trust actually is (settlor, trustee, beneficiaries), why the super-rich go to islands like the Cayman Islands, Jersey, the BVI and the Cook Islands, how layers of trusts and companies make ownership disappear, where the line sits between tax avoidance and tax evasion, what the Panama and Pandora Papers revealed, and why one of the world's biggest hiding places is now in America, in South Dakota. title: The Vancouver Model: How Drug Money Became Houses
views_per_day_limitation: Snapshot views divided by age at retrieval; not a historical velocity series.
description:
July 2015. A casino just outside Vancouver accepts $13.5 million in cash in a single month, almost all of it in $20 bills, much of it carried in by the bagful. Upstairs, a surveillance analyst watches it on his monitors. He is looking at one piece of something much bigger. Investigators would later give it a name: the Vancouver Model.

In this video we take that machine apart, one piece at a time. What money laundering actually is: placement, layering and integration. How two very different problems, piles of drug cash in Vancouver and money that couldn't leave China, ended up solving each other through underground banking. How casino cash moved into real estate, why almost half of Vancouver's most expensive homes had hidden owners, and what an expert panel estimated it did to home prices. Then: why nobody stopped it for years, and how the Peter German reports and the Cullen Commission finally changed the rules.

description:

In this video we open up the machine. Where Social Security came from and the story of Ida May Fuller, the very first monthly check. title: What If Your Money Grew 10x Every Day?

description:
In 2013, a man opened his PayPal statement and saw a balance of $92 quadrillion. It was a glitch. But what if it wasn't? What if you had a magic wallet that made your money 10 times bigger every single night?

Start with $1. By day 6 you're a millionaire. By day 9, a billionaire. By day 15 you'd have more than the entire world is worth. And that's exactly where the story stops being a fantasy and starts teaching you how money really works: exponential growth, why money isn't wealth, the Cantillon effect, hyperinflation in Germany, Zimbabwe and Hungary, compound interest, Warren Buffett's real secret, and why Ponzi schemes always promise growth that sounds like magic.

title: Why You’ll Never Actually Spend Your Retirement Savings

description:
Ronald Read pumped gas, worked as a janitor and held his coat together with safety pins. When he died in 2014, he left behind about $8 million. He saved a fortune and spent almost none of it. And he wasn't that unusual.

We save for forty years so we can spend it in retirement. But real retirees don't follow the plan: the typical retiree with $500,000+ still has nearly 90% of it after twenty years. In this video we break down why: the fear of outliving your money, the saver's brain and loss aversion, why a monthly paycheck gets spent but a pile of savings doesn't, the annuity puzzle, required minimum distributions, and the go-go, slow-go and no-go years of retirement.

title: Your Money Isn't in the Bank. So Where Is It?
views_per_day_limitation: Snapshot views divided by age at retrieval; not a historical velocity series.
description:
In the 1660s, a banker in Stockholm was sentenced to death for printing too much money. Today every bank in the world does exactly what he did, thousands of times a minute, and it's completely legal.

So when you put $100 in a bank, where is it? Not in a vault. In this video we break down how commercial banks really create money when they make loans, why that money disappears when the loan is paid back, what happened during the Northern Rock bank run of 2007, and what a giant stone at the bottom of the sea has to do with your bank balance.
